rationale: The candidate is a coherent early-stage massing with a readable dominant stepped bar and a clear hierarchy between a broader base and reduced upper volume. Across all four views the form stays consistent, so it avoids the common multi-view collision failure. The stepped profile is not arbitrary stair-steps; it behaves like a continuous cascading mass, which suits the legacy silhouette metric. Programmatically it can plausibly hold a compact neighborhood-living/commercial hybrid: the linear bar is compatible with a capacity-aware street building, and the setback creates some upper terracing. The main weakness is the access edge response: the blue frontage edge is met more by a sealed/compressed side than a strongly public ground void, so void_publicness is only moderate. The internal notch/cut is visible but not yet fully legible as a public court or entry seam. Overall, the mass is salvageable and program-fit, with the main improvement needed being a clearer street-facing void or undercut aligned to the verified access edge.
